# P37.68d — consolidated operator walkthrough packet: all 13 journeys + the U-003.1…11 surface

**Status:** REQUESTED — never simulated. This packet is the agent-prepared
input to the **operator's own walkthrough** (OP-22; recorded
`operator walkthrough (maintainer, not independent)` — TS-22). Nothing on
this page is a result; the operator's walk is the only walkthrough that
counts, and it lands in the operator's own record.

**When:** the live window is `on the promoted P37.65 release; 390 px +
1440 px` (the plan cell, verbatim). The promoted release does not exist
yet — `D-P37.65b-1` (the promote leg) is QUEUED behind the operator's
HG-11 readout. This packet is staged so the walk can start the moment the
release promotes.

**Scope:** the consolidated walk — all 13 D3 journeys (advocate A1–A4,
journalist J1–J5, organizer O1–O4) plus the U-003.1…11 per-ask surface.
The per-journey steps and pass clauses are the sibling packets' own
(`p37.68a-capstone/WALKTHROUGH.md`, `p37.68b-capstone/WALKTHROUGH.md`,
`p37.68c-capstone/WALKTHROUGH.md`) — this packet consolidates them into
one record table; the per-ask section names the extra spot-checks the
operator's eye adds on top of the agent battery.

**Labels:** every agent result is recorded `agent-verified` — a machine
walkthrough, never user research and never "user-tested" (P4,
SIG-UI-077/078).

## Setup (operator)

1. The promoted release origin: `<promoted-origin>` — the URL P37.65b's
   promote leg publishes (fill in at walk time; never guessed).
2. Viewports: **1440 px** and **390 px** browser widths (any tool —
   responsive-design mode is fine).
3. JavaScript **on** for the primary legs; **off** where the journey
   allows a no-JS leg (browser site settings or dev-tools toggle). The
   journey batteries name each journey's no-JS allowance.
4. A fresh, cold start at `/` for each journey — walked like a reader,
   not an operator who knows the routes.
5. Timeboxes per K13 §8 and the sibling packets.

## Per-ask spot-checks (operator's eye — U-003.1…11)

These are the human-readable halves the agent battery cannot judge —
readability, trust, obviousness. Fill one line per ask; a "?" is an
honest answer.

| ask | one-line check | verdict (operator) | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| U-003.1 | the map reads as a real place, not a demo tile | | |
| U-003.2 | labels are names a person said aloud, never identifiers | | |
| U-003.3 | a search that fails says so, plainly | | |
| U-003.4 | the place list reads like geography, not a database dump | | |
| U-003.5 | "from N sources" is believable at a glance | | |
| U-003.6 | a dossier's picture and its search box answer the same place | | |
| U-003.7 | /watch answers "what changed" without jargon | | |
| U-003.8 | /evidence shows artifacts a person could download | | |
| U-003.9 | the sources table is scannable; gated rows read as gated | | |
| U-003.10 | one source page tells its whole story | | |
| U-003.11 | the research queue asks for help without pretending it sent anything | | |
